newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian firms in lawless Albania plead for support.
newsitem.headline: Italian firms in lawless Albania plead for support.

text.p: Italian entrepreneurs hit by violence in Albania on Thursday made an urgent plea for financial support from the Italian government, saying many of them were on the brink of bankruptcy.

"Sadly, only a lot of solidarity has come up to now to our 150 looted and damaged (Italian) enterprises," businessman Luigi Fabri, head of an Italian entrepreneurs committee, told a news conference here.

He said that only by keeping and creating jobs in Albania, Europe's poorest country, could Italy curb Albanian attempts to flee and provide a element of stability. Over 10,000 Albanian refugees are estimated to have fled to Italy since March.

Italy is Albania's biggest investor and trading partner, with 300 billion liras invested by private firms who directly employ over 100,000 of Albania's 3.4 million population, the group said in a statement.
Overall, they estimated damages suffered by Italian enterprises in widespread rioting in March at 70 billion lire.
For example, Coca-Cola Bottling Enterprise Tirana Shpk, majority-owned by Italy's Busi Group, said it had lost one- third of its market when the south of the country spun out of government control.
Fabri said only one-third of 800 Italian firms had remained operational.
"Many businesses are on a razor's edge in the sense that they will close down if financing does not arrive," Fabri said.
Many Italian businesses in Albania were not insured ahead of the crisis, and a Tirana lawyer said not even Albanian insurers were covering losses caused by the unrest.
Parliamentary elections, seen as crucial to stop the violence which has claimed more than 1,500 lives, are planned for June 29 despite increased security concerns.

But an Italian businessman producing garments in Tirana said his workers, mostly women, were still putting in irregular hours and had even refused to work in the period between the June 29 first round and run-offs on July 6.
